article_title: Banks Shift AI Agent Liability to Customers as Regulators Weigh Who Pays When Agents Overstep
summary: Automated checks passed; manual review found two quote-fidelity issues and one quantifier overstatement in subordinate body content (not the headline/summary/lead), correctable with a public corrections note.

findings.message: Fabricated direct quote attributed to Julia Leung; source presents this as indirect speech, not a quotation.
findings.details: Body text reads: Securities and Futures Commission CEO Julia Leung said separately, "Human review of every intermediate step would be unrealistic," favoring oversight calibrated to how much autonomy an agent has. The cited PYMNTS source (source-3.html.gz, 'Regulators Converge on Twin Compliance Challenges From AI Agents') contains no quotation marks around this phrase; the raw HTML reads: 'Securities and Futures Commission CEO Julia Leung acknowledged that human review of every intermediate step would be unrealistic.' This is PYMNTS' indirect paraphrase of Leung's remarks, not a direct quotation. The submission converts it into a verbatim quotation with quote marks, misattributing exact words to Leung that the source never quotes her as saying.

findings.message: Filburn quote conflates an actual direct quotation with the reporter's unquoted follow-on sentence, and drops the opening clause of the real quote.
findings.details: Body text reads: Chris Filburn ... argued that "liability should lie with whoever is best equipped to prevent the harm or loss in the first place. In this case, it's the AI provider." The cited PYMNTS source (source-4.html.gz, 'Panel Weighs Who Pays When AI Agents Exceed Consumers' Instructions') raw HTML reads: '“From a legal and policy perspective, liability should lie with whoever is best equipped to prevent the harm or loss in the first place,” Filburn said during the discussion. In this case, it’s the AI provider.' Only the first sentence is inside quotation marks in the source (and it opens with 'From a legal and policy perspective,' which the submission omits without an ellipsis); the second sentence ('In this case, it's the AI provider') is the reporter's own unattributed gloss, not quoted. The submission presents both sentences as a single verbatim Filburn quotation.

findings.message: Quantifier overstatement: article says Anthropic's contrast is a point 'several of these stories flag', but only one of the five cited sources mentions Anthropic at all.
findings.details: Keyword search across all five decompressed source snapshots for 'anthropic' (case-insensitive) found 3 matches in source-0 (TechCrunch) and zero matches in source-1 (Decrypt), source-2, source-3, and source-4 (all PYMNTS). Only TechCrunch discusses Anthropic's read-only personal finance tool; no other cited source mentions Anthropic. 'Several of these stories flag' overstates source support for that framing.

content_preview.title: Banks Shift AI Agent Liability to Customers as Regulators Weigh Who Pays When Agents Overstep
content_preview.summary: Citi, JPMorgan, Bank of America, PNC and Citizens Bank updated terms shifting AI-agent account risk to customers, as the OCC, the Fed and Hong Kong regulators debate liability rules.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

AI agents that can log into a bank account, read transaction history, and in some cases pay bills or move money have moved from novelty to a live operational problem for retail banks. According to [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/383677/citi-customers-responsible-ai-banking-agents-rogue-hack), the trigger was a banking security scare on October 22, when major banks detected AI agents logging into customer accounts, sometimes taking steps that appeared to go beyond what users had instr...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Analysis with Background / Current situation / Implications sections that cleanly separate sourced facts from editorial synthesis. Neutral tone throughout, no sensationalism, no AI self-reference. 1,528 words, within the 800-2000 Analysis band.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 source snapshots in sources/2026-11/banks-shift-ai-agent-liability-to-customers-as-regulators-weigh-who-pays-when-agents-overstep/ were read in full after gunzip, and sha256 of each decompressed file was independently recomputed and matched the manifest: source-0.html.gz (TechCrunch, e2ba53ed...) confirms Citi/JPMorgan/BofA/PNC/Citizens claims and the verbatim Citi spokesperson quote and the Anthropic 'read-only'/'can't move, manage, or invest your money' quotes; source-1.html.gz (Decrypt, 1ac765e0...) confirms the October 22 security-scare trigger, PNC's operational restrictions, the CFPB non-waiver position, and that PNC's change and TechCrunch's report both landed on a Wednesday; source-2.html.gz (PYMNTS OCC, 49e5b3d1...) confirms the Nov 4 OCC bulletin scope and Boyd/Polsinelli's documentation guidance; source-3.html.gz (PYMNTS regulators, c0f7b1c9...) confirms Barr's Milan remarks, Chan's verbatim 'algorithm has no license to lose' quote, and the HKIMR 13%/56% figures, but shows the Leung line is NOT a direct quote in the source (see findings); source-4.html.gz (PYMNTS panel, b7b08b51...) confirms the McWilliams, Alper and Chen quotes verbatim and the Visa 42.8% figure, but shows the Filburn quote in the submission merges an actual quotation with the reporter's unquoted gloss and drops its opening clause (see findings). suspicious_patterns was null for all 5 manifest entries; no prompt-injection content found. Independent-source count for the Analysis requirement: 5 of 5 cited outlets (TechCrunch, Decrypt, and 3 PYMNTS pieces) are independent of the banks and regulators named in the article — easily clears the 2-independent-of-4 minimum. Anthropic disclosure: required - the article devotes a dedicated paragraph to Anthropic's own read-only banking-agent product as an explicit contrast point to the five banks' policies, which triggers the policy's 'passage of its own naming Anthropic' test; the required one-sentence disclosure ('The Machine Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic.') is present immediately after that paragraph and does not characterize Anthropic's product beyond what TechCrunch states.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: The headline, summary, and lead are fully supported: the five named banks' policy changes and the OCC/Fed/Hong Kong regulatory activity are all confirmed in the source snapshots. The writer's self-reported correction was verified and holds up: the body text explicitly scopes Citi's 'customer-authorized even after a credential leak' language and Citi's self-exemption carve-out to Citi alone ('Of the policies detailed in the sources reviewed here, Citi's is the most sweeping... JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citizens Bank moved in a similar direction without the same level of reported detail'), rather than generalizing Citi's specific contractual language across all five banks. Two subordinate quote-fidelity problems were found and are detailed in findings/corrections: (1) the Leung line is presented as a verbatim quotation when the source only paraphrases her remarks indirectly; (2) the Filburn quotation incorporates the reporter's unquoted follow-on sentence and drops the quote's actual opening clause. A separate quantifier overstatement claims 'several' sources flag Anthropic's contrast when only one (of five) does. All three issues sit in subordinate body paragraphs, not the headline, summary, or lead, and are each independently and honestly coverable in a single corrections record. One soft inference worth flagging but not correcting: the body states PNC 'changed its terms the same day' as Citi 'per TechCrunch' — TechCrunch describes Citi's change as happening 'this week' and PNC's as happening 'today' (its Nov 18 publish date) without explicitly asserting they fell on the identical calendar day; Decrypt independently confirms PNC changed on Wednesday (Nov 18) but does not pin down Citi's exact day either. This is a plausible but not fully sourced inference; it does not rise to the level of a correction because no source contradicts it and it is not a specific, falsifiable number or quote.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; presents competing views (bank terms vs. consumer-protection law vs. panelists' disagreement on who should bear liability) without editorializing.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-11/ for overlapping coverage of banks, AI-agent liability, or the OCC/Fed/Hong Kong regulatory threads; found no prior Machine Herald article on this topic. This is a genuinely new story, not a duplicate or rewrite of existing coverage.
concerns: Leung quote: presented as verbatim ('Human review of every intermediate step would be unrealistic,') when the cited PYMNTS source only paraphrases her indirectly ('Leung acknowledged that human review of every intermediate step would be unrealistic'). No quotation marks exist around this phrase in the source.

Filburn quote: the submission's quotation merges PYMNTS' actual quoted sentence with an unquoted follow-on sentence ('In this case, it's the AI provider') and silently drops the real quote's opening clause ('From a legal and policy perspective,').
Anthropic quantifier: 'a contrast point several of these stories flag' overstates source support — only 1 of 5 cited sources (TechCrunch) mentions Anthropic.
recommendations: Future submissions should treat PYMNTS' 'X acknowledged/said that...' indirect-speech constructions as paraphrase, not verbatim quotation, even when the underlying sentence reads naturally as a quote.
When a quote spans a reporter's quoted sentence plus an unquoted editorial follow-on, quote only the sentence that is actually inside quotation marks in the source.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong Analysis: well-sourced, clearly organized into fact/analysis sections, correctly scopes Citi's sweeping liability language to Citi alone rather than generalizing it across all five banks, and carries a correctly-placed Anthropic disclosure. Two subordinate direct-quote fidelity problems (Leung, Filburn) and one quantifier overstatement (Anthropic 'several') were found in the body, none in the headline/summary/lead, each independently and honestly summarizable in a single corrections record. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, well-sourced Analysis of a developing bank/regulator liability dispute for a defined fintech/policy-focused audience, but not a broad-audience or industry-defining story.
